subject.title: [Bug]: openclaw status falsely reports openclaw-mem0 memory as unavailable when the live gateway plugin is working

question: Should memory status/deep use live gateway memory-runtime health as the source of truth, or is the current `not checked` behavior sufficient for external memory plugins?
rationale: Current main only softens the misleading wording, while the issue request, the open conflicting fork PR, and the broader open issue require a maintainer-owned decision about the permanent status boundary.

options.title: Use the broader live-gateway contract
options.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 the canonical implementation path, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

options.title: Revive the fork PR
options.body: Ask the fork PR author to rebase, resolve conflicts, and prove human and JSON status output against a real external memory plugin without local startup side effects.

options.title: Accept `not checked` as enough
options.body: Declare the current shipped wording sufficient, close the conflicting fork PR, and close this issue with release evidence.

recommendation.title: Use the broader live-gateway contract
recommendation.body: Make https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/62599 the canonical implementation path, close or replace the conflicting fork PR, and require live external-memory proof before closing this issue.

likelyOwner.reason: The product boundary spans status UX and plugin runtime ownership, and steipete has the strongest history signal on both the shared status scan and memory-runtime plugin routing changes.
